title: Clipboard writes can no-op if user gesture activation is lost before they run
answers: Why does clicking 'Copy link' sometimes not actually copy anything?
Copy-to-clipboard button silently fails after a dropdown/menu closes
navigator.clipboard.writeText does nothing in some browsers
body:
Symptom: clicking a 'Copy link'/'Share' control inside a menu sometimes copies nothing, with no error, especially right after the menu closes.
Root cause: navigator.clipboard.writeText() requires an active user gesture at call time; if the write is deferred (e.g. after async menu-close logic) the browser silently drops it. public/app/core/utils/explore.ts:copyStringToClipboard previously called writeText directly.
Fix pattern: prefer navigator.clipboard.write([new ClipboardItem({'text/plain': Promise.resolve(value)})]) synchronously inside the click handler — ClipboardItem accepts a Promise so the async part doesn't need the gesture to still be live, only the initial call does. Always feature-detect (typeof ClipboardItem !== 'undefined' && navigator.clipboard?.write) and require window.isSecureContext before using it, falling back to writeText then to a hidden textarea + document.execCommand('copy').
Constraints: only applies to clipboard writes triggered from UI event handlers where activation timing is uncertain (menu items, async handlers); plain synchronous button clicks with writeText are usually fine. Clipboard API (including ClipboardItem) is unavailable outside secure contexts (non-HTTPS/non-localhost), so the execCommand fallback must be kept.
applies: Any UI in the Grafana frontend that copies text to the clipboard, especially from menus/dropdowns or after async work
